tickets.title: Delivery e-bike storage and sidewalk obstruction at 11th Street
tickets.requester: Susan Cestor (District Manager); Joshua Wu (public speaker); Alejandro Torres (public speaker)
tickets.summary: Dozens to over 100 electric delivery bikes used by food delivery workers are stored on the sidewalk and street at 11th Street and First Avenue every day and night, blocking sidewalks, hurting nearby businesses and landlords, and raising fire-hazard concerns. The 9th Precinct plans an enforcement action on October 7 that would confiscate improperly parked bikes, and speakers asked for advance notice, translated warnings, and tagging instead of seizure. Action: Board and district office to follow up on the October 7 enforcement, confirm workers receive multilingual notice, and help find a legal parking or corral site for the bikes.

tickets.title: Drug activity and dark spots in Seward Park and Tompkins Square
tickets.requester: Susan Cestor (District Manager); Troy (public speaker); Niles Robinson (liaison, Manhattan Borough President's office)
tickets.summary: Residents and park groups report increased drug use, homelessness, and needles around Seward Park, the Lower East Side Ecology Center, and nearby restrooms, and say poorly lit dark spots in the park help hide drug use. The district manager says police have been stationed in Seward Park under a task force, which has shifted activity to Tompkins Square Park, and the office is following up with the Seventh Precinct. Action: Board and district office to ask the precinct and Parks Department for a coordinated plan beyond moving activity between parks, and for 311 reports on out lights to be followed up with Parks and DOT.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP and community market protections
tickets.summary: The Land Use and Economic Development joint committee reviewed the EDC request for proposals for the Essex Market, which was due out by the end of this month. EDC could not clearly say whether the board's two resolutions on keeping the market community-focused had been included. Action: Board to get EDC to postpone issuing the RFP and confirm the resolutions' terms are included, with a clarifying meeting planned this week.

tickets.title: Liquor license application at 11 Allen Street
tickets.summary: The operator of a former Time Again location applied for a full liquor license at 11 Allen Street, a location that is unlicensed and near Dime Square and a temple. The committee had voted 3 to 2 for a conditional recommendation with limited hours and no DJs, but the full board voted 20 to 10 with 9 abstentions to recommend outright denial. Action: Board to organize community members to attend the State Liquor Authority hearing to support the denial, since the SLA can approve without the board's stipulations.

tickets.title: Free public restrooms pilot in Delancey and Cooper Square
tickets.requester: Transportation committee chair (unnamed); Niles Robinson (liaison, Manhattan Borough President's office)
tickets.summary: The city is installing 17 free public restrooms citywide as a one-year pilot, with two in the district at Delancey Plaza and Cooper Square and East Sixth Street and Third Avenue, expected mid-October. Concerns were raised about access, who can use them, and emergency calls. Action: Board to pass a resolution next month setting out access rules and the next steps during the pilot year.

tickets.title: Canal Street redesign update and Manhattan Bridge exit safety
tickets.summary: A letter was sent to the mayor and DOT restating the board's concerns about the Manhattan Bridge exits after a recent fatal crash. The letter also asked for an update on the Canal Street redesign, since the board has had no update since January. Action: Board and district office to follow up on DOT's response and press for the Canal Street redesign update.

tickets.title: Proposed closure of Third Avenue L train stop
tickets.summary: A public speaker who built a simulation from MTA trip data argued that closing the L train's Third Avenue stop would save New Yorkers about 1,800 hours a day, since only about 5% of riders board or leave there and the stop is not accessible or a transfer station. He asked the board to refer the idea to the transportation committee and to propose a pilot closure with the MTA. Action: Board to refer the proposal to the transportation committee and consider asking the MTA for a pilot closure of the Third Avenue stop.

tickets.title: Mobile voting option for CEC elections
tickets.requester: Health and Human Services committee (unnamed presenter)
tickets.summary: Turnout in Community Education Council elections has been about 2% over multiple cycles, partly because many households rely only on smartphones and some parents are not signed into the NYC schools account. The resolution asks the Department of Education to pilot a mobile-first voting option alongside in-person voting, with multilingual outreach and clear eligibility messages that address immigration-related fears. Action: Board to send the resolution urging the DOE to pilot mobile voting and expand outreach to parents, and to take back the concerns about immigrant families to the provider.

tickets.title: Proposed bylaws changes on attendance and removal
tickets.summary: The bylaws committee presented proposed changes that would create an earlier attendance process, with a letter and an executive committee meeting after excess absences, separate attendance from the removal process, and apply conflict of interest policies to public members. A member raised a concern that the removal recommendation process has two steps and may be a double recommendation. Action: Board to vote on the bylaws changes at the October full board meeting, with notice sent at least 28 days before.

tickets.title: District needs statement and October budget priority vote
tickets.summary: The board will vote in October on its district needs statement and ranked expense and capital budget priorities for city agencies, drawing on committee work and meetings with about 20 agencies. The district manager noted that the draft housing plan had 7,000 units over five years, but 75% are market rate, while the board's top need is affordable housing. Action: Board to vote on the district needs statement and ranked budget priorities in October, with the affordable housing need emphasized.
